title: Colorimetric Iron Quantification Assay
author: Natalie Rubio
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.x2ufqew

steps.title: Equilibrate reagents and thaw probe
steps.instruction: Bring the iron standard, iron assay buffer, and iron reducer to room temperature; thaw the iron probe and keep it on ice for the duration of the assay (≈1 h).

steps.title: Prepare iron standard dilutions
steps.instruction: Dilute 10 µL of iron standard in 990 µL distilled water to make a 1 mM stock; set up a standard‑curve dilution series in a 96‑well plate and allocate duplicate wells (2 × 100 µL each).

steps.title: Process tissue samples for assay
steps.instruction: Use fresh tissue or thaw snap‑frozen tissue on ice (≈2 h total); weigh 10 mg per condition, wash in cold PBS, homogenize each piece in 300 µL iron assay buffer with a Dounce homogenizer on ice (15 passes), transfer homogenates to microcentrifuge tubes, centrifuge at 16,000 × g for 10 min, then move the supernatants to clean tubes and keep on ice.

steps.title: Add standards and samples to plate
steps.instruction: In a 96‑well plate, add 100 µL of each standard dilution in duplicate; add 50 µL of each tissue supernatant in quadruplicate (duplicate for Fe²⁺, duplicate for total Fe) and supplement with 50 µL iron assay buffer to reach 100 µL total volume per well.

steps.title: Add reducers and incubate at 25°C
steps.instruction: Add 5 µL iron reducer to each standard well; for Fe²⁺ wells add 5 µL assay buffer, and for total‑Fe wells add 5 µL iron reducer; mix gently and incubate the plate at 25 °C for 30 min.

steps.title: Add iron probe and incubate
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL iron probe to every well (standards and samples), mix, then incubate at 25 °C for 60 min in the dark.

steps.title: Measure absorbance at OD 593
steps.instruction: Read each well on a colorimetric microplate reader set to absorbance 593 nm.

steps.title: Analyze data and calculate iron
steps.instruction: Average duplicate readings for each standard and sample; subtract the mean absorbance of the blank (standard 1) to obtain corrected values; plot corrected absorbance versus known iron concentrations and fit a line (y = 0.0826x + 0.0199, R² = 0.9987); determine Fe²⁺ and total Fe from the curve, compute Fe³⁺ by subtraction, and calculate sample iron concentration using [C] = (Sa/Sv) × D (Sa = nmol Fe in well, Sv = µL sample added, D = dilution factor; Fe atomic weight = 55.845 g mol⁻¹).
